reasoning: The underlying problem—whether textual prompts can offset/override an injected steering vector—is substantially worked. "Belief Dynamics" (arXiv:2511.00617) formally shows in-context prompts and activation steering combine additively in log-belief space, so an opposing prompt shifts/offsets the steering curve, but it deliberately avoids refusal/safety tasks (uses dark-triad personas) and never frames it as adversarial neutralization. "Steering Safely or Off a Cliff?" (2602.06256) and "Probing the Robustness of LLM Safety to Latent Perturbations" (2506.16078) directly study robustness of inference-time safety steering to perturbations including prompts, and "(Un)Reliability of Steering Vectors" (2505.22637) documents 29-43% "anti-steerable" samples where adversarial inputs defeat/reverse steering. However, no single paper runs the exact proposed experiment—holding an injected refusal vector fixed, searching prompt prefixes/suffixes/role-play frames, and reporting a prompt-only "neutralization success rate" on a harmful-request benchmark—so the specific safety-framed adversarial angle and its quantitative metric remain an open gap, while the core robustness question is largely answered.

evidence.title: Belief Dynamics Reveal the Dual Nature of In-Context Learning and Activation Steering
evidence.summary: Proves prompts (ICL) and activation steering combine additively in log-belief space on Llama-3.1-8B/Qwen-2.5-7B/Gemma-2-9B, so an opposing prompt predictably shifts (and could offset) the steering curve. Directly relevant theoretical answer, but tests dark-triad/nihilism personas, not refusal/safety, and never frames it as adversarial neutralization—leaving the proposal's safety angle open.

evidence.title: Steering Safely or Off a Cliff? Rethinking Specificity and Robustness in Inference-Time Interventions
evidence.summary: Directly studies robustness of inference-time safety steering interventions to adversarial/prompt-level manipulation, citing refusal-mediation and jailbreak literature. Concerns whether steering loses robustness to simple prompt manipulations—closely overlapping the proposal's question.

evidence.title: Probing the Robustness of Large Language Models Safety to Latent Perturbations
evidence.summary: Probes robustness of LLM safety to latent/activation perturbations and introduces an Activation Steering Attack; studies whether small activation/representation shifts re-trigger harmful behavior, overlapping the robustness-of-safety-steering theme.

evidence.title: Understanding (Un)Reliability of Steering Vectors in Language Models
evidence.summary: Documents that 29-43% of samples are 'anti-steerable' (shift opposite to the intended steering direction) and that adversarial inputs can defeat or reverse steering effects—evidence that the proposed neutralization phenomenon already occurs and is measurable.

evidence.title: Activation steering robustness to prompt variations (search synthesis)
evidence.summary: Beyond Prompt Engineering / related robustness work reports that 'steering is robust to prompt variations... effectiveness remains unaltered' in some settings while jailbreak-prefixed harmful queries can amplify compliance—showing the prompt-vs-steering robustness question is actively studied with mixed published answers.

evidence.title: Jailbreak steering generalization
evidence.summary: Community work on mean-difference jailbreak/refusal steering vectors and their interaction with prompt-based jailbreaks; establishes that the difference-of-means refusal-vector + jailbreak-prompt interaction is already explored, though not as a prompt-only neutralization-rate study against a fixed injected vector.
